config.title: Image Gallery

intro.title: Image Gallery
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build an interactive image gallery component using Vue. You'll learn how to manage a collection of images with reactive state, allowing users to navigate through them. The core concept involves using Vue's reactivity system to track the current image index and update the display automatically. You'll work with key Vue constructs like ref for state management, computed properties for derived values, and event handlers for user interactions. By the end, you'll have a functional gallery that responds to button clicks to cycle through images.
intro.usecase: Image galleries are foundational UI patterns used across countless real-world applications. You'll find them in e-commerce product displays, social media feeds, portfolio websites, and photo management apps like Google Photos. As a Vue developer, you'll frequently build galleries for dashboards that visualize data, content management systems that handle media uploads, or interactive catalogs with filtering capabilities. Mastering this pattern teaches you how to manage dynamic data collections, implement responsive layouts, and create engaging user experiences that are essential for modern web development.

objectives: Construct a Vue component that renders an image gallery with a grid layout
Initialize and bind reactive state to manage the current image selection
Implement click handlers to update the displayed image when thumbnails are selected
Configure computed properties to dynamically generate image sources and alt text
Integrate conditional rendering to display image details only when an image is selected
Manipulate CSS classes dynamically to highlight the active thumbnail
Apply Vue directives to iterate through an array of image data and render gallery items

steps.title: Define prevImage handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named prevImage that decrements the currentIndex value, wrapping to the last image when at the beginning (index 0).
steps.hint: Inside the script setup, after the nextImage handler, create a function that checks if currentIndex is 0 and sets it to images.length - 1, otherwise decrements it by 1.
steps.seedCode:
<template>
  <!-- Add your component structure here -->
</template>

<script setup>
// Import Vue and ref from 'vue'
import { ref } from 'vue';

// Initialize reactive images array here
const images = ref([
  { id: 1, src: 'image1.jpg', alt: 'Mountain landscape' },
  { id: 2, src: 'image2.jpg', alt: 'Beach sunset' },
  { id: 3, src: 'image3.jpg', alt: 'City skyline' }
]);

// Create currentIndex reactive state here
const currentIndex = ref(0);

// Define nextImage handler here
function nextImage() {
  if (currentIndex.value === images.value.length - 1) {
    currentIndex.value = 0;
  } else {
    currentIndex.value++;
  }
}

// Define prevImage handler here
</script>
steps.expectedOutcome: The prevImage function will allow navigating backward through the gallery images with wrap-around behavior.
successCriteria: A function named prevImage is defined that properly handles decrementing currentIndex and wrapping to the last image when at index 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your logic. Make sure the function wraps to the last image when currentIndex is 0, and decrements otherwise.
steps.feedbackWrong: The prevImage function isn't defined correctly. Remember to check if currentIndex is 0 and handle the wrap-around case.
